what_it_does: This chip is a high-speed communications transceiver for routing data over long cables in data center networks. It uses a 4-level encoding scheme (PAM-4: each signal state represents two binary digits) to pack more information into each clock cycle. The design uses 5-nanometer transistor technology and achieves 212.5 gigabits per second throughput while consuming only 2.2 picojoules (trillionths of a joule) per transmitted bit. The key challenge addressed is compensating for signal degradation (over 46 decibels of loss) that occurs when data travels through cables, connectors, and packaging components. This allows data center operators to use longer cables between servers without losing reliability.
